item.research_question: How can cryo-rolling and annealing be utilized to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in multiphase high entropy alloys, specifically regarding the development of a hierarchical microstructure?
item.processing_route: Multi-pass cryo-rolling up to ~90% reduction in thickness with immersion in liquid N2 for 45 minutes before and after each pass, followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 hour and water quenching.
item.test_conditions: Tensile tests at ambient temperature with an initial strain rate of 8.3 × 10−4 s−1; Nano-indentation with load increased linearly from 1 μN to 500 μN over 0.25 seconds.
key_findings: The cryo-rolled and annealed material achieved a Yield Strength (YS) of 1437 ± 26 MPa and Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) of 1562 ± 33 MPa.
The elongation to failure (ef) was approximately 14 ± 1%, which remained almost unchanged compared to the as-cast material (17 ± 1%).
The hierarchical microstructure consists of fine lamellar regions with ultrafine FCC grains (average size ~200–250 nm) and coarse non-lamellar regions with coarse unrecrystallized B2 phase (~2.5 µm).
The hardness of the B2 phase (~12 GPa) is nearly three times higher than that of the L12 phase (~4 GPa) in the as-cast material.
The cryo-rolled and annealed material covers the entire hardness spectrum with softer regions (≤8 GPa), intermediate regions (~8–12 GPa), and much harder regions (≥12 GPa).
The cold-rolled and annealed material showed a homogenous microduplex morphology with grain sizes of ~0.5 µm, unlike the heterogeneous cryo-rolled structure.
The cryo-rolled and annealed EHEA possesses the highest YS and UTS while maintaining appreciable ductility compared to other HEAs like Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi and Fe40Mn27Ni26Co5Cr2.
item.mechanism: The simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility originates from a characteristic hierarchical microstructure that creates profuse domain boundaries separating domains of different hardness, leading to significant back stress strengthening and delayed necking due to strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs).
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: The hierarchical microstructure of the cryo-rolled and annealed material resulted in simultaneous enhancement in strength (Yield Strength/YS: 1437 ± 26 MPa, Ultimate Tensile Strength/UTS: 1562 ± 33 MPa) and ductility (elongation to failure/ef ~ 14 ± 1%)
The relative hardness difference of the two phases during cryo-rolling (ΔHcryo) should be much higher than that during cold-rolling (ΔHcryo ≫ ΔHcold).

The existence of strain gradients in heterogeneous materials with different hardness domains should be associated with significant back stress strengthening, which should delay necking during tensile loading and improve strength and ductility.
